A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SwissGov-RSD research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–J are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-annotation analyses and experiments evaluating encoders and LLMs on SwissGov-RSD and iSTS-RSD, including Table 3 and supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model experiments and reports revised annotation analyses and SwissGov-RSD evaluation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same DiffAlign algorithm, few-shot prompting, LLM fine-tuning, encoder regression architecture and loss, and LLM-based label projection. The annotation revision does not introduce a new automatic detection method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 224 multi-parallel Swiss government documents covering EN-DE, EN-FR, and EN-IT, together with the same iSTS-RSD languages and augmentation scenarios. Revised annotations do not expand or remove represented documents, domains, or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix experiments: the same DiffAlign encoders, prompted and reasoning LLMs, fine-tuned LLMs, and ModernBERT variants participate. LaBSE's parameter-count correction does not establish a comparator replacement.

E3.justification: Section 3 reports replacing a poor EN-DE annotation run with a new annotator, substantially revising reference annotations used for evaluation. Table 2 also adds agreement over all token labels, including zeros, alongside existing span-based metrics. Model training budgets, dataset sizes, and testing procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 revises the analysis of model sensitivity to annotator differences and removes v1's Figure 9 case study illustrating missed omissions/additions. The span-granularity examples in Figure 8 remain. The token-position analysis in Figure 5 is updated, while the projected-label audit and other supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimation. Table 15 retains the same 100 encoder and 10 LLM timing measurements. The added human-agreement correlation is an evaluation metric.

E6.justification: SwissGov results and rankings change substantially. In Table 3, the EN-DE leader switches from Qwen3-Embedding 4B at 16.1 to LaBSE at 20.6, previously 12.5; Llama-3.1 405B changes from 2.4 to -0.8. Revised EN-DE references prevent interpreting these as same-setting model gains or losses. XLM-R+SimCSE's EN-FR and EN-IT scores also change from 9.3/24.6 to 10.0/23.4. Tables 2, 6, 7, and 14 and Figures 3, 5–7 contain revised results; iSTS-RSD scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, labeling definitions, IoU equation, and DiffAlign equation are unchanged. Applying the existing Spearman metric to all human labels introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: a first naturalistic document-level cross-lingual RSD benchmark and a substantial performance gap between synthetic and realistic evaluation.

C2.justification: Section 3 replaces the earlier emphasis on exceptionally poor EN-DE span agreement with a distinction between span overlap and label consistency. Section 6 adds document segmentation as a possible explanation for short-context encoders' stronger results. Appendix A.4 removes the explicit ranking-instability warning and the interpretation concerning missed omissions/additions.

D1.justification: v2 documents the annotation-run replacement and its reported agreement improvement in Section 3, footnote 6. Table 10 corrects LaBSE's stated parameter count from 500B to 500M. Prompts, annotation guidelines, hyperparameters, hardware and timing information, and code/data access links otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kreutzer et al. (2020) and Lavie et al. (2025) to contextualize annotation difficulty. The retained Sarti et al. (2025) citation shifts from supporting ranking-instability concerns to contextualizing agreement. The broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in annotation validation, the encoder/LLM discussion, and Appendix A.4, with small wording and header edits elsewhere. The overall section organization, methods exposition, and principal contribution narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with adjusted chart sizing and axes presentation. Table 2 regroups its metrics and adds an agreement row. v1's omission/addition Figure 9 is removed; its Figure 10 becomes v2's Figure 9, and Appendices B and C now share a page. These are localized presentation changes.

improvement.justification: Replacing the poor EN-DE annotation run addresses a serious consistency weakness in the paper's central benchmark. On the overlapping documents, English-side IoU rises from 11.17 to 23.98 and German-side IoU from 10.22 to 39.95 (Table 2). Reporting all-token human agreement also makes model results easier to contextualize. Removing Appendix A.4's ranking-instability warning weakens qualification, but the substantial annotation-quality repair and stronger validation outweigh that loss.
